page.layout: One printed page (right page of the opening). One text column, full height, with running head and page number at the top. A narrow margin on the right holds one note at the level of the line "patentibus". Left of the text is the edge of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: tētia enim 27. Imperatorem hortatur, vt sibi ipsi imponat necessitatem leges observandi, rationem subnectit; quia non habet in terris qui ipsum possit cogere. Certé si in terris habuerit qui ipsum possit iudicare, possit deponere, possit interficiendum mandare, habuisset qui possit cogere; sed illa hercle Agapeto doctrina prorsus fuit incognita, licét Romano Pontifici, homini inprimis cordato, & insigniter erudito: Romano, inquam, Pontifici, aufim confidenter dicere, licét Pontificij moderni (his se confossos sententiis tanquam pugionum ictibus sentientes) de eo ambigat; sed qua nixi ratione prorsus non video; cum omnes illius Pontificis circumstantiae, huic nostro Diacono belle quadret, nec quicquam impedit Diaconum hunc, vt illum Pontificem Romanis ortum patentibus,{q} in sua Paraenesi Attico (vt loquitur q? Baronius) & exculto sermonis genere, Graecum referat. Cum ex Historijs constet etiam, Agapetū Papam cum Graecis fuisse versatissimum, vt pote qui à Theodato Rege (sue Reginae Amalasunthae afsasino) missus ad Impera-torisIn appen-dice ad tom.7.

page.notes: The word "tētia" at the start and the numeral "27" beside it are copied as best as I can read; the spacing in "2 7" is uncertain. The mark "q" after "loquitur" is doubtful, marked [?]. The small "O" printed on the last line, left of "toris", is not a word and is left out; "toris" completes "Impera-toris". The reference mark "q" in the text is matched by the margin note with the same letter. Long s is copied as s throughout. The "1" of the printed note marker in "loquitur" was read as a "q" with a query.
